meta.title: Agent loop gate model
meta.description: Machine-readable description of the gate lifecycle (ADR-010 G1-G8). Prepared, not normative. Until the cutover decision (Epic-008 L1), ADR-010 is the authoritative source.

issueTypes.rule: Does not carry the label epic.

vocabulary.description: Set (a): the admissible gate-mode label vocabulary from ADR-010 G8. Exact names, no aliases.

unknownMembers.note: Classification ignores unknown needs:* labels except for duplicate detection (evaluator-compatible diagnosis). The actionGuard result blocks every consumer action while one is present (fail-closed, Epic-008 L4/L6).

families.note: In gate mode, status:* is admissible only as one of the two shared terminal exits. Any other status:* label is a work status.

unknownMembers.note: role:planner is a mode conflict (gate-with-legacy-role); other unknown roles only produce role drift.

vocabulary.foreignLabels: Labels outside all families are foreign and ignored by every rule.

legacyStatuses.description: Set (b): ADR-009 statuses, used only to recognise legacy issues (ADR-010 G1). No legacy semantics are modelled (Epic-008 L4).

outputCodes.description: Set (c): every code a classification result can contain. roleActual echoes input labels and is therefore not a code.

serialization.holds: Present holds in the fixed order needs:operator, needs:replanning, needs:upstream, joined with ','; 'none' if empty.
serialization.roleActual: Suffixes of all role:* labels, sorted by code point, joined with '+'; 'none' if empty.

cardinality.description: Cardinality per family on an open gate issue (ADR-010 G8). enforcement=classification means the contract table rejects violations; enforcement=diagnostic means a violation is reported as role drift only.

rules.rule: valid prefix of the task chain
valid prefix of the parent chain

rules.note: A missing or wrong role label is not a prefix error and alone does not block a claim (ADR-010 G8).

invariants.rule: Every gate present requires all earlier gates of the same type's chain.
Only the next gate of the chain may be added.
invariants.enforcedBy: transition static prechecks (topGate equals the predecessor)

invariants.rule: Regular withdrawal removes gates from the highest downward until all remaining statements are currently true.
A task with gate:activated or a parent with gate:promoted, gate:implemented or gate:accepted is invalid.
An OPEN gate issue without terminal must carry at least gate:created.

conditionLanguage.description: Decision tables are ordered; the first row whose 'when' holds wins. Conditions are defined in schema/gate-model.schema.json ($defs/condition): has, count, duplicates, state, value, sameValue, always, and the combinators all, any, not. Labels are counted per occurrence; a GitHub label set never contains duplicates, only evaluator-sequence inputs do.
conditionLanguage.selectors: A selector picks labels of the input: by family (members all | known | unknown), by an explicit label list, by the named set legacyStatuses, or a union (anyOf).
conditionLanguage.derivedValues: Derivations are evaluated in the listed order; later ones may reference earlier ones by name, result fields by dotted path (e.g. modeResult.outcome).

derivations.name: roleExpected
derivations.description: Role projection, precedence from top to bottom.

rows.note: Only reachable for a CLOSED issue without gates and without terminal.

derivations.name: roleDrift
derivations.description: Drift is a diagnosis, not an error.

derivations.name: modeResult
derivations.description: Mode classification. Precedes every terminal, claim or contract check.

derivations.name: contractResult
derivations.description: Contract classification of a gate issue.

rows.note: Only reachable with inputKind evaluator-sequence; a GitHub label set has no duplicates.

derivations.name: pool
derivations.description: Contractually admissible claim pool. Only meaningful when contractResult.outcome is ok.

rows.note: Task accepted, parent activated, or no gate.

derivations.name: actionGuard
derivations.description: Consumer safety check, independent of the three classification results and without evaluator counterpart. A consumer offers no write and no claim unless actionGuard.outcome is ok. An unknown needs:* label may be a hold this model version does not know; it is treated as blocking (fail-closed, Epic-008 L4/L6).

claimPools.description: Pools a claim may reserve (ADR-010 G4). A pool is a static admissibility statement, never a claim and never an authorisation.

pools.reservation: separate co-architect slots up to the fixed quorum; not the main architect of the same round
no agent work; operator waiting point
one exclusive dev claim, only with exec:agent
one exclusive QAT claim by a reviewer independent of the coder
only the responsible main architect, for re-spec work
no claim: not OPEN, terminal set, blocking hold, task accepted, parent activated or no gate

holdEffects.effect: blocks all agent claims; leaves the projected role unchanged; removed only by the operator
blocks all agent claims; leaves the projected role unchanged; removed by the operator only after documented fulfilment of the external precondition
blocks coder and reviewer; allows only re-spec work by the responsible main architect; projects role architect

minimumMaturity.rule: An issue with only gate:created and no maturity:* may be claimed for the draft by master architects only.

ruleTextOnly.text: Before a review round the main architect fixes a quorum of one to three independent co-architect PASS. Changing spec or quorum starts a new round and voids earlier PASS for the decision.
Only valid PASS of the current round from independent agent/listener identities count. A shared GitHub bot account does not prove independence.
A listener/agent pair is configured by repo, role and maximum maturity; claims above the own maturity are excluded.
Claims are time-limited reservations, not gates. Lease, timer and retry mechanics are implementation decisions.
A claim whose gate disappeared is orphaned: it may not be taken over; its holder stops delivery and gate writes and may only release and comment.
Coder and reviewer claims of the same delivery must never be valid at the same time.

externalPreconditions.description: Preconditions labels cannot prove. They are named, not evaluable. A consumer offers a write only after checking them via the authoritative write path; if any is unknown, the write is not offered (fail-closed).

catalog.text: The actor is the operator, proven by auditable provenance. role:operator grants no operator right.
The actor is the responsible main architect of this issue.
The reviewer is independent of the coder of this delivery.
Repo, role and maturity fit of the actor's capability.
The actor holds the valid draft claim.
The fixed quorum of independent co-architect PASS for the current spec round is reached.
The actor holds the exclusive dev claim.
The actor holds the exclusive QAT claim.
A running QAT claim is released or invalidated before the gate withdrawal or before the head/evidence changes.
Affected claims are halted or invalidated before their gate preconditions are withdrawn.
All claims are released; if that fails, the terminal write does not happen and a visible diagnosis is given.
The current delivery (PR head or no-PR evidence) is completely and verifiably submitted.
The PASS is bound to exactly the same head or no-PR evidence as gate:implemented.
The PR is merged or the no-PR evidence is verified (finished), or the abort is deliberate (abandoned).
For a parent, the operator has checked goal and children.
A justified reason is documented on the issue.
Fulfilment of the external precondition is proven and the decision documented.
A separate operator go for gate start exists; before it, no gate issue is created.
After the separately proven legacy creation stop, the creation time must be provable; an unclear creation time leads to an operator handoff.
gate:promoted was set by the operator, proven by auditable label provenance; a shared bot account proves nothing.
No concurrent change happened between read and write; GitHub label operations are not atomic and there is no compare-and-swap.

role-projection.text: After a gate write, the gate write path corrects role:* to the projection, with readback. Skipped under mode-conflict (no workflow write at all) and under prefix-invalid (role stays unchanged). Gate and role write are not atomic.

readback.text: Re-read issue state and labels and re-classify; the result must match the intended state.

remove-roles.text: An issue with terminal carries no role:*; operator handoff happens by comment/notify, not by a role label.

close-issue.text: Final means CLOSED, exactly one terminal and no claim.

transitions.description: Label transitions of a gate issue. staticPrecheck is at most a necessary static pre-check over classification results; it is never an authorisation (Epic-008 L5). globalPrecheck applies in addition to every staticPrecheck and every exception. Every transition additionally requires its externalPreconditions.

items.note: mode:gate is set at creation and never changed; mode is never inferred from gate labels. The architect or operator creates gate issues (operator decision).
Exactly one maturity:* is required from drafted on, so the maturity is set before this write.
The ADR-009 operator override is not inherited; an exception needs its own operator/ADR decision.
Execution release for exactly this spec. exec:* is fixed before promotion.
Operator-only no-PR task: the operator sets implemented with evidence; an independent reviewer checks afterwards.

triggers: change of head or no-PR evidence after submission (coder)
items.note: gate:promoted stays. The coder improves the same delivery / PR and resubmits.

triggers: parent goal, guardrail or completion-rule change
any other loss of the current spec
items.note: Gates are withdrawn top-down before the body changes; a new spec/review round starts, and promotion or activation is again an operator gate. The existing PR stays the working state of the same delivery unit. Known implementation difference: the write path refuses a cascade across an operator gate; L8 exception requested.
A change of exec:* with existing promoted first requires withdrawing promoted and the delivery gates, then a new operator promotion.

A maturity change is a spec change: it voids the current review round; specified and dependent gates are withdrawn first (withdraw-specified). Replacing the label takes two non-atomic writes; from drafted on, the intermediate state is cardinality-invalid until readback. Known implementation difference: the write path sets maturity only when advancing to drafted and refuses later changes; L8 exception requested.

The architect or operator sets execution before promotion (operator decision). Known implementation difference: the write path sets exec only when advancing to specified and refuses a change without revoke; L8 exception requested.
Only after the current spec round and an independent quorum carry specified again; then the operator may promote again.

exceptions.text: An unexpected non-prefix stops every interaction fail-closed and leads with diagnosis to needs:operator. This hold is the only workflow write admissible under prefix-invalid.

items.note: Under mode-conflict no workflow write happens at all, not even a hold (comment/notify only).
Releasing a hold also requires the full mode/prefix/claim check.
All roles may set needs:upstream; only the operator releases it (operator decision).

ruleNotes.text: The terminal write requires no additional gate precondition; it checks only unambiguous mode, terminal uniqueness and release of all claims. It is therefore admissible from any contract result as long as the mode is gate.
No gates are coded as a precondition for abandoned.

items.note: The operator restores a valid prefix; afterwards readback must classify ok before roles are projected and needs:operator is released.
An OPEN issue with terminal requires recovery by the operator and no agent work; handoff by comment/notify.
